thread:
aj: Heads up — noticed apiserver p95 in eu-south spiked to ~2.3s right after the GPU onboarding wave. controller-manager leader election happened twice in 3m. etcd raft append latency also bumped. anyone else seeing this? :thinking:
priya: Seeing it too. Graphs show DNS flaps in the same window, high NXDOMAIN and intermittent coreDNS restarts. Could be kube-proxy conntrack exhaustion during the onboard surge.
aj: Timeline: GPU pool scaled +120 nodes at 02:14 UTC, first apiserver spike at 02:16. controller-manager restart at 02:18. etcd leader stepdown at 02:20.
jamie: Logs look like slow proxy syn backlog then apiserver 502s. kube-proxy conntrack count nears ephemeral port limit. On hosts: conntrack shows many TIME_WAIT from gpu-less pods.
morgan: We also saw kubelet oom on some init containers on the onboard nodes — they restarted and flooded the control plane with node add events.
lee: If kubelet churn + DNS flaps + conntrack hits, apiserver watch cache likely thrashes. Suggest throttling onboarding and set admission controller burst lower.
priya: Agreed. I've throttled the provisioning pipeline to 10 nodes/min and disabled aggressive burst for this batch. Monitoring now.
aj: Oncall-bot triggered pages for apiserver-high-latency -> triggered runbook step 1.
oncall-bot: pagerduty incident PD-3492 created by aj. Runbook: check etcd state, restart coreDNS if needed, throttle provisioner.
jamie: Quick checks:
```
# etcd raft entries/sec
curl -s http://etcd-metrics:2379/metrics | grep raft
# conntrack summary
sudo conntrack -S | grep tcp
```

jamie: etcd leader append-duration histogram shows tail at 700ms in that window.
morgan: coreDNS indeed restarted 3 times, logs show upstream DNS timeouts to the VPC resolver. Network team — any peering blips around 02:15?
lee: I see a short peering jitter. Cloud provider notes 'transient route flap' in eu-south 02:14-02:17. That aligns.
priya: Actions taken: throttled onboarding, scaled up coreDNS replicas from 2->4 in eu-south, bumped controller-manager leader-election-duration to be a bit more forgiving, and increased conntrack_max on kube-proxy nodes as a stopgap.
aj: Nice. Do we need a rollback of the wave? Risk is continued thrash and cost. What's current CPU/util and node add rate?
jamie: Node add rate down to ~6/min from 25/min. apiserver p95 back to 220ms after coreDNS scale and throttle. etct latency trending down.
morgan: I'm patching the provisioner to watch conntrack headroom before spinning new batches, will open PR.
lee: Suggest a postmortem to capture: (1) combined failure modes (dns + conntrack + kubelet oom), (2) default probe/limits on init containers, (3) provisioner backoff heuristics, (4) possible network-level mitigations with provider.
aj: I'll file incident and link PRs. For now keep the wave paused and watch for regression for 30m. :thumbsup:
priya: I'll keep monitoring logs and metrics, will ping if anything changes.
oncall-bot: PD-3492 status: acknowledged by priya.
jamie: Follow-up: add a health-check gating in the prov pipeline: require conntrack headroom > 30% and coreDNS endpoints ready before next batch.
morgan: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/provisioner/pull/482. includes gating + backoff. tagging @aj @priya for review.
aj: Reviewing now. thanks all — good catch.
